name: water
summary: Full-bleed hero running Paper Shaders' water on WebGL2: waves and caustics refracting a deep blue-teal gradient the section paints for itself, with that same gradient as the CSS resting state.

colors.description: Four blooms painted into the source gradient the water refracts. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette.

speed.description: Rate the surface moves. 0 renders a single static frame. Forced to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion.

waves.description: Depth of the wave distortion applied before the image is sampled.

caustic.description: Strength of the caustic light banding riding over the surface.

deviations.why: defaultPreset fits the source image with `contain` at scale 0.8, which centres a small framed picture in the section. abstractPreset is upstream's own full-bleed variant (fit cover, scale 3), so the values are still upstream's, just the preset built for this job.

deviations.what: The source image is generated in the page rather than supplied by the caller: four soft blooms in the --fx-c* palette painted to a canvas and handed over as a data: URI.
deviations.why: The shader mixes its output toward `texture(u_image, uv)` weighted by that texel's alpha, so with no texture bound the sampler reads opaque black and the whole hero renders flat. It genuinely needs an input, and a generated site must fetch nothing off-site, so the section paints its own from the same custom properties the CSS resting state uses.

deviations.what: The GLSL that actually runs is @paper-design/shaders 0.0.80's water shader, which differs from the pinned commit in two lines: upstream guards the layering term with `if (u_layering > 0.)`, and multiplies the highlight mix by `u_colorHighlight.a`. The vendored build does neither.
deviations.why: vendor/paper.js is the published 0.0.80 bundle (see vendor/PROVENANCE.md), and the port imports the shader from it rather than carrying a copy, so the vendored build is the one that ships. Checked line by line against the pinned commit: god-rays, metaballs, dithering and liquid-metal match it exactly; water is the only one that does not. Neither difference is reachable at our defaults -- abstractPreset sets layering 0, and colorHighlight is opaque #ffffff -- but a caller who raises `layering` or passes a translucent highlight gets 0.0.80's behaviour, not the pinned commit's.
